newsitem.title: USA: Williamsburg, Va., urged to issue $10 million GOs.
newsitem.headline: Williamsburg, Va., urged to issue $10 million GOs.

text.p: The financial adviser for Williamsburg, Va., recommended the city issue $10 million of general obligation bonds to fund most of its fiscal 1997 capital improvements, Daily Press reported Friday.
David Rose, managing director of Wheat First Butcher Singer, urged the city to issue the bonds by the end of the year. The city council will review the recommendation Sept 12, the newspaper said.
Although Williamsburg has usually relied on pay-as-you-go financing, City Manager Jackson Tuttle said "Some degree of financing appears to be a reasonable option."

The city plans about $14 million of capital projects in fiscal 1997, including $4 million for its share of a courthouse being built jointly with James City County, $2.75 million for its share of a regional jail, and a $2.25 million library expansion.
